content: Misfortune enters through the mouth; disease enters through the mouth.
author: Chinese Proverbs
sourceWork: Huo cong kou chu, bing cong kou ru (祸从口出，病从口入) — Fu Xuan
explanation: The mouth is humanity's most perilous portal. What we swallow in excess poisons the organs and brings sickness; what we blurt out in haste sparks feuds and brings ruin. Guard what enters your lips with moderation, and what exits your lips with vigilance.
practicalInsight: Practice mindful eating and mindful speech today: eat only until eighty percent full, and speak only what builds up.
reflectionPrompt: In what ways has indiscipline in speech or physical diet recently eroded your vitality or peace?
